Generative models have shown a significant decline in the accuracy of deepfake detectors over recent years, with detection rates falling from 99.5% to 76%. This decline raises issues regarding the reliability of content authenticity verification, as even advanced detection methods struggle against sophisticated adversarial attacks, leading to a concerning loss in post-hoc verifiability of images created by these models.

 - Deepfake detection accuracy has decreased significantly from 99.5% to 76% over the last four years.
 - Adversarial perturbations can reduce detector accuracy to below 2%, complicating verification of authenticity.
 - The unreliability of current methods indicates that content alone cannot reliably determine authenticity.

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05870
